text.p: A rain interruption left
second seed Goran Ivanisevic close to a 7-6 (7-5) 4-1 victory
over Australian Jason Stoltenberg in the second round of the
$1 million RCA tennis championships on Tuesday.
The Croatian, winner of two titles this year and a 4-2
leader in the career series with the world No. 60 Australian,
had taken control of the contest when the rain hit.
A mid-day thunderstorm stopped play for 90 minutes.
Nearly two-and-a-half after the rain began, officials
finally called the contest off until Wednesday.
The match between fifth-seed Carlos Moya of Spain and
American Steve Campbell also was rained out.
Two minor seeds stumbled to upset losses on a day when a
thundertorm interrupted early play.
Australian Richard Fromberg, normally more at home on
European clay, knocked out Spanish 11th seed Alberto
Berasategui 5-7 7-6 (7-5) 6-1, and world No. 243 Californian
Glenn Weiner beat No. 15 Thomas Johansson of Sweden 6-7 (6-8)
Even getting into the event was a surprise for the
21-year-old Weiner, who won his first ATP Tour match last
month at home in Los Angeles.
"I was in Brazil playing a Challenger when I got a fax
under the hotel door saying I'd been awarded this wild card,"
the American said. "It was pretty unbelievable, it's one of
the greatest things I've received."
Chris Woodruff, seeded 12th, stopped inexperienced
American compatriot Justin Gimelstob 3-6 6-4 6-1.
Woodruff dropped his lost his opening set, but recovered
to frustrate the 20-year-old Gimelstob, touted as one of the
few top prospects of the next generation for the Americans.
Gimelstob exploded with a yell of joy as he briefly took
the lead in a late game, but that was a brief moment of glory
for the world No. 91.
